Honestly, the scene was tailor-made for those who deal with the devil.

On Wednesday's episode of The Daily Show, host Josh Johnson pointed out a detail from Donald Trump Jr.'s wedding that looks like it was lifted straight from a hit horror film — and you can't unsee it once you do.

Johnson first aired a clip Trump Jr. shared on social media from his wedding to socialite Bettina Trump, held in May on a small island in the Bahamas, before delivering his killer punchline.

The footage, set to a guitar version of The Ronettes' "Be My Baby," opens with an aerial shot of the church where President Donald Trump's eldest son held his ceremony, then shows the interior with guests. The clip shows Trump Jr.'s siblings Ivanka and Tiffany Trump seated in the pews, followed by slow-motion footage of the bride and groom embracing at the altar beneath a massive cross.

Johnson cracked: "What a beautiful wedding ceremony, in that church from Sinners." As he said it, he displayed a still from the Oscar-winning film in which Sammie (played by Miles Caton), covered in blood, walks into his father's church. Directly above Sammie's head — just like above Don Jr. and his bride — hangs a massive cross. The exterior of the church in Sinners bears a strong resemblance to the one in the Bahamas.

The wedding had already come under intense scrutiny after ProPublica reported that Donald Trump Jr.'s wedding was funded by Russian oligarch Umar Kremlev, who has close ties to President Putin.

Amid the uproar, Bettina Trump issued a statement on Instagram clarifying: "Don and I got married privately on Friday with just our family."

She continued: "The weekend that followed had been planned long in advance as a fun weekend with friends. It was never intended to serve as our wedding weekend. When our original wedding plans changed, we simply decided to get married earlier and arrive at the already-planned weekend as a newly married couple."

She also wrote that the couple's "dear friend Umar very generously hosted two wonderful nights of celebrations for us after we were married."

Johnson had a rather hilarious response to Bettina Trump's clarification.

Johnson, mimicking Bettina Trump's tone, said: "Yes, that's right, fake news. They didn't pay for my wedding — they just paid for a much more expensive victory party."
